about: Codex accounting fixtures. CodexAccountingFixtureTests (Swift) and scripts/test_codex_accounting_replica.py (Python replica) both write each case's files under an empty Codex home and must report exactly `expected`: per local day, per model, [input, cached, output]. Scan as of now_utc with days_to_scan. Line shapes follow real Codex rollouts; every value is invented. Timestamps sit between 11:00 and 13:00 UTC so the local day is the same in any time zone within 11 hours of UTC. Each line is written as compact JSON, one per line.

cases.name: parent_and_two_subagents
cases.description: A parent rollout and two subagent rollouts. The subagents carry the parent's session_id and their own payload.id; each counts. Keying files on session_id drops both subagents.

cases.name: empty_shell_then_real_file
cases.description: Two files of one thread (same payload.id): the first by path has no token events, the second holds the thread's usage from a counter starting at zero. Both count. Keeping the first file per payload.id keeps the empty one and drops the usage.

cases.name: continuation_without_overlap
cases.description: One thread continued in a second file a day later, its counter starting again from zero. The two files' events do not overlap in time, so both count.

cases.name: byte_identical_copy
cases.description: The same rollout under sessions/ and, byte for byte, under archived_sessions/. Their events overlap exactly, so it counts once.

cases.name: fork_with_inherited_counter
cases.description: A fork whose cumulative counter continues its parent's: its first event reports the parent's 5000 input plus its own 700. The inherited 5000 is not counted again.

cases.name: copied_history_before_meta
cases.description: A subagent file that begins with a copy of its parent's history, the parent's session_meta and token events, stamped before the subagent's own session_meta and with no history ordinal. Only the events after it are the subagent's.

cases.name: counter_goes_down_and_back
cases.description: The cumulative total falls from 200 to 150 and climbs to 300. The baseline stays at 200, so the file counts 300 in all, not the 350 that re-counting the climb from 150 gives.

cases.name: repeated_total
cases.description: The same cumulative total reported three times in a row adds nothing after the first; summing last_token_usage instead would count the request three times.

cases.name: counter_restart_counts_only_above_the_old_high
cases.description: The counter restarts inside the file (the total drops to one request's own usage). The baseline only rises, so requests after the restart count only once the total passes the old high of 2000: 1000 + 1000 + 400. This undercounts a genuine restart; it is the price of never counting a replayed lineage twice.

cases.name: last_usage_only
cases.description: Events that carry only last_token_usage (no cumulative total) count as reported.

cases.name: continuation_that_carries_its_counter_over
cases.description: One thread continued in a second file whose counter picks up where the first file's ended: its first event reports the first file's 5000 input plus its own 1500. The files do not overlap, so both count, and the carried-over 5000 is counted once.

cases.name: copied_history_marked_by_ordinal
cases.description: The shape Codex writes: a subagent file whose copy of the parent's history is stamped after the subagent's own session_meta, so its times say nothing. The session_meta's subagent_history_start_ordinal names the first line of the subagent's own history; the copied token events before it are not counted.

cases.name: partial_overlap_both_count
cases.description: Two files of one thread whose event spans overlap without one containing the other (11:01-11:20 and 11:15-11:40), each with events the other lacks. Neither is a copy, so both count; dropping one for merely overlapping would lose its usage.

cases.name: archived_prefix_of_live_file
cases.description: An archived copy taken while the thread was still running: the first two events of the live file. Its span lies within the live file's, so only the live file counts.

cases.name: migrated_subagent_counts_its_own_work
cases.description: The shape Codex's migration of an older subagent rollout leaves: the history boundary (subagent_history_start_ordinal) is the file's line count, so every line is numbered before it, and no ancestor session_meta was copied in. The boundary marks nothing here; the file holds the subagent's own work and counts. Treating the boundary as a copy marker drops it all.

cases.name: migrated_subagent_skips_the_replayed_parent_tail
cases.description: A migrated subagent rollout (boundary at the file's line count, no ancestor session_meta) that begins by replaying the parent's last request, stamped after the subagent's own session_meta, before the parent's first inter-agent message to it. Token events before that message are the parent's and are not counted; the subagent's counter continues from the replayed one, so its first own event counts only its own request. Counting the replayed event counts the parent's 2500 again.

cases.name: migrated_subagent_without_an_inter_agent_message_counts_in_full
cases.description: A migrated subagent rollout (boundary at the file's line count, no ancestor session_meta) with no inter-agent message: nothing marks a replayed prefix, so every event counts.

cases.name: gap_over_last_counts_the_growth
cases.description: Between two token events the cumulative total grows by more than the second event's own last_token_usage: a turn was aborted after its request, and that request wrote no token event of its own. The app counts the total's growth (4000 input by the second event); counting last_token_usage there, as CodexBar does, leaves the aborted request out.

cases.name: interleaved_lineages_count_the_higher_only
cases.description: Two cumulative counters alternate in one file (1000, 300, 1800, 600, 2500). The baseline only rises, so the lower counter's events are skipped and the file counts the higher counter's growth, 2500. CodexBar switches after the first fall to counting the smaller of each event's own usage and the growth contained under its high mark, so it can differ here; this pins the app's choice.

cases.name: continuation_that_replays_the_previous_tail_counts_it_twice
cases.description: KNOWN LIMIT, pinned so that changing it is a visible decision. Two files of one thread whose event spans only touch (11:01-11:10 and 11:10-11:40): the second begins by repeating the first file's last event, then continues. Neither span lies within the other, so both files count, and the repeated request (1500 input) is counted in each: 4600 instead of 3100. No such pair was found on the machine this was measured on; removing repeated events across files needs per-event keys, which the cache does not keep.
